title: Pipeline-stage-aware token provenance and split-billing for multi-step inference flows
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Modern Redwood customers frequently build multi-stage inference pipelines (normalize -> embed -> rerank -> summarize). Different stages can be executed by separate internal services or third-party tools; some stages are transient (previews) while others produce billable artifacts. Right now we bill at a coarse-grained request boundary which leads to two problems: (1) double-charging when the same tokens are re-encoded by downstream stages; (2) mis-attribution when intermediate stage costs should be billed to the pipeline owner rather than the original caller. This ticket defines a provenance-first metering design to enable split billing across pipeline stages and to avoid duplicate token charges for re-encodings.
background: Recent customer support cases and audits revealed discrepancies when customers plug Redwood rerankers or summarizers into third-party orchestration layers. Example: a client pretokenizes and sends a compact representation; the orchestration layer expands it and calls our embed endpoint, then calls generate with the same expanded prefix. Without stage-aware provenance, both the embed and generate flows attribute full input token counts to the initial requestor, plus the intermediate service, creating confusing invoices. Existing tickets (metering for compressed attachments, reranker candidate aggregation) reduce some duplication but don't provide a cross-stage provenance model.
goals: Record token-level provenance metadata per logical pipeline stage so we can attribute costs to the correct billing entity
Detect and dedupe re-encodings of the same logical prefix across stages to prevent double-charging
Expose a split-billing ledger that can apportion costs across pipeline participants (caller, pipeline owner, 3rd-party connector)
Integrate with quota enforcement so per-entity quotas reflect only their true consumption
non_goals: Change tokenizer semantics or model-level charge calculation (we still count tokens using canonical tokenizer for model)
Rewrite existing billing pipelines end-to-end in this ticket (this is an incremental compatibility layer)
design_proposal: 1) Introduce a lightweight token-provenance header on public API requests: X-RW-Token-Provenance (opaque id + optional stage metadata).2) When a request enters a pipeline stage, if the upstream stage provided a provenance id, the stage includes it in the downstream request; the runtime attaches a canonical fingerprint for the normalized token sequence (SHA256 of canonicalized whitespace + token IDs).3) Metering pipeline will store ledger entries keyed by (fingerprint, provenance-id, stage-id). If a fingerprint appears with the same provenance across stages within a 30-minute window, downstream costs for re-encodings will be flagged for dedupe and only the first occurrence is billed to token-consumer quota; subsequent occurrences can be billed to pipeline-owner metadata or zeroed depending on policy.4) New split-billing metadata fields (bill_to_entity, payer_percent) will be supported in the request envelope for customers who want explicit cost apportionment.5) Quota checks will be run against the billing entity identified by bill_to_entity; fallback to original caller when absent.6) Backwards compatibility: if no provenance header is present, we fall back to current behavior (bill to requestor).
acceptance_criteria: E2E integration test that creates a 3-stage pipeline (client pretokenize -> embed -> generate) and demonstrates no double-charge when the same canonicalized prefix is processed twice
Audit API that can return ledger entries for a given fingerprint across stages
A migration runbook that explains how to update connectors to emit X-RW-Token-Provenance and handle new split-billing fields
Documentation in Console explaining how split billing is presented on invoices and per-route dashboards
Load tests show <2% CPU overhead on metering path at 50k rps with caching enabled
risks_and_mitigation: Fingerprint collision (low): use SHA256 + canonicalization and include tokenization scheme version in fingerprint to avoid cross-model collisions
Gaming by replaying provenance ids to avoid charges: enforce signed provenance tokens (HMAC) for private deployments and rate-limit unknown provenance ids
Storage growth for per-fingerprint ledger: keep TTL of 7 days by default and allow enterprise customers to opt into longer retention

Edge-case: when different tokenizers (model family) produce different token sequences for same text; mitigation: include tokenizer-version and model-family in fingerprint and only dedupe when they match
implementation_tasks: API: add X-RW-Token-Provenance header parsing and validation (ENG-SEC- TBD for signing scheme)
Runtime: compute canonical fingerprint at ingestion layer and pass through metering pipeline
Metering service: add dedupe lookup table + rules engine for split billing application
Billing: extend ledger schema with fingerprint and provenance_id fields; add query path for split billing summaries
Console: display per-stage cost split on per-request traces and billing UI
Tests: unit tests for fingerprint canonicalization; integration tests for multi-stage flow; load tests
progress_updates: 2026-03-11: Spike completed — validated canonicalization approach with a small corpus. Found tokenizer-version drift between gpt-family and rwt-family needing to be part of fingerprint (Aisha).
2026-03-12: Prototype header format and HMAC signing wire-up; security reviewed signing approach and requested enterprise opt-in (Diego).

2026-03-13: Implemented runtime fingerprint calculation in staging; added in-memory dedupe cache and exercised 3-stage integration test. Observed a 0.9% p99 latency increase on the metering path. (Diego)
2026-03-14: Meeting with billing to finalize ledger schema changes and retention policy (Liam Chen from Billing). Planning migration PR next week.
open_questions: Default policy for downstream re-encodings: should we zero-charge subsequent occurrences or bill them to pipeline-owner by default? (Product decision)
What TTL for dedupe entries balances correctness vs. storage cost for SMB customers?
How to present retroactive credits if we detect duplicate charges during audit?
notes: This is intended to be an opt-in compatibility layer initially: customers can enable split-billing and provenance emission via route-level config. Over time we may recommend connectors emit provenance by default.
